ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: \textit{As shown in the figure, in an equilateral $\triangle ABC$, $BD$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, point $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and point $P$ is a movable point on $BD$. Lines $PE$ and $PC$ are drawn. When the value of $PE + PC$ is at its minimum, what is the degree measure of $\angle EPC$?}
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and BD is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, \\
therefore, point D is the midpoint of AC, and BD$\perp$AC, \\
thus, points A and C are symmetric with respect to BD, \\
as shown in the figure, draw AE, intersecting BD at P, the length of line segment AE is the minimum value of PE+PC, \\
since point E is the midpoint of side BC, \\
thus AE$\perp$BC, \\
since $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, and BD is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, \\
thus $\angle PBE=30^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle BPE=60^\circ$, \\
since in $\triangle BPE$ and $\triangle CPE$, \\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}PE=PE \\ \angle PEB=\angle PEC=90^\circ \\ BE=CE \end{array}\right.$, \\
therefore, $\triangle BPE\cong \triangle CPE$ (SAS), \\
therefore, $\angle EPC=\angle BPE=60^\circ$. \\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{60^\circ}$.

Since BD is the angle bisector from B, it passes through the midpoint of AC, so its equation is y=x/sqrt(3). Write P=(t,t/sqrt(3)). Then PE+PC equals sqrt((t-1)^2+t^2/3)+sqrt((t-2)^2+t^2/3). This one-variable sum of distances along a line is minimized at t=1, equivalently where BD meets the vertical line AE. Thus P=(1,1/sqrt(3)). Now vectors from P are PE=(0,-1/sqrt(3)) and PC=(1,-1/sqrt(3)). Their dot product is 1/3, while |PE|=1/sqrt(3) and |PC|=2/sqrt(3). Hence cos angle EPC=(1/3)/((1/sqrt(3))(2/sqrt(3)))=(1/3)/(2/3)=1/2. Therefore angle EPC=60 degrees.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in an equilateral $\triangle ABC$, $BD$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, point $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and point $P$ is a movable point on $BD$. Lines $PE$ and $PC$ are drawn. When the value of $PE + PC$ is at its minimum, what is the degree measure of $\angle EPC$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and $BD$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, therefore point $D$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $BD \perp AC$. Thus, points $A$ and $C$ are symmetric with respect to $BD$. As shown in the figure, draw $AE$, intersecting $BD$ at $P$; the length of line segment $AE$ is the minimum value of $PE+PC$. Since point $E$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, thus $AE \perp BC$. Since $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, and $BD$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, thus $\angle PBE=30^\circ$, therefore $\angle BPE=60^\circ$. Since in $\triangle BPE$ and $\triangle CPE$, $PE=PE$, $\angle PEB=\angle PEC=90^\circ$, and $BE=CE$, therefore $\triangle BPE\cong \triangle CPE$ (SAS). Therefore, $\angle EPC=\angle BPE=60^\circ$. Hence, the answer is $\boxed{60^\circ}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; D is on side AC, line segment BD goes from B through interior point P to D; E is on the base BC; PE and PC are drawn in the figure.
Reasoning: From the problem statement, ABC is an equilateral triangle, and BD is the angle bisector of angle ABC, so BD is one of the axes of symmetry of the equilateral triangle, and point A and point C are symmetric with respect to BD. Therefore, for any point P on BD, PC = PA. Thus, to make PE + PC minimal is equivalent to making PE + PA minimal. According to the shortest reflected path, at the minimum A, P, E are collinear, that is, P is the intersection point of AE and BD. Also because E is the midpoint of BC, in an equilateral triangle AE is perpendicular to BC, so PE is perpendicular to BC, and triangle BPE is right-angled at E. Because angle ABC = 60°, and BD bisects angle ABC, angle PBE = 30°. In right triangle BPE, angle BPE = 180° - 90° - 30° = 60°. Also E is the midpoint of BC and PE is perpendicular to BC, so PE is the perpendicular bisector of BC, B and C are symmetric with respect to PE, therefore angle EPC = angle BPE = 60°.
